text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. An API allows your program to communicate with another service by sending HTTP requests, usually using methods like GET or POST. Most APIs return data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Before you can access protected data, you often need authentication, such as an API key or a token. It is also important to respect rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make within a certain time. Finally, always include error handling in your code, because network problems and invalid responses can happen at any time.
